articles.title: IIT Madras Pravartak opens free online training for Classes 7–12
articles.summary: IIT Madras Pravartak is offering free live online programmes for school students and educators during its November 2026–January 2027 cycle. Student topics include AI fundamentals, electric vehicles and future mobility, entrepreneurship, design thinking and innovation.
body: IIT Madras Pravartak, the institute's technology innovation hub, has announced free live online training programmes for school students and educators. The programmes are being offered in collaboration with BodhBridge Education.

For students in Classes 7 to 12, the announced learning areas include artificial intelligence fundamentals, electric vehicles and future mobility, entrepreneurship fundamentals, design thinking and innovation. The programme cycle covers November 2026 to January 2027.

The organisers say the sessions will be delivered by people from the institute's alumni network, start-up community and industry. An optional certificate is available. Interested students and educators should check the official registration portal for current course availability and conditions.

articles.title: Kerala announces 2027 SSLC and Plus Two examination schedule
articles.summary: Kerala's 2027 public examination schedule places SSLC exams from 1 March and Higher Secondary first- and second-year exams from 2 to 30 March. The state expects more than 13 lakh candidates across its public examinations.
body: Kerala has announced the schedule for its 2027 public examinations. The Secondary School Leaving Certificate (SSLC) examinations are scheduled to begin on 1 March 2027, while Higher Secondary first- and second-year examinations are scheduled from 2 to 30 March.

The announced timetable also places SSLC information technology practical examinations in February, followed by model examinations later that month. Evaluation of SSLC answer scripts is scheduled to begin in April, with results expected in May.

The state expects more than 13 lakh students to appear across SSLC, Higher Secondary and other public examinations. Students should confirm their individual subject dates and any later changes through the relevant Kerala examination authority.

articles.title: CAT 2026 to introduce AI facial-recognition checks at exam centres
articles.summary: IIM Indore says candidates taking CAT 2026 will undergo an AI-based facial match as part of identity verification. Physical admit-card checks will continue, and the institute says the system will not store a student database.
body: Candidates appearing for the Common Admission Test (CAT) 2026 are expected to undergo an AI-based facial-recognition check at examination centres. IIM Indore, which is conducting this year's test, says the technology is being introduced to help match candidates with the photographs submitted during registration.

The institute has said that the existing physical verification of admit cards will continue alongside the technology. The system is being tested for accuracy, and the institute's director has stated that a database of students will not be stored.
CAT 2026 is scheduled for 29 November. Candidates should follow the instructions on their admit cards and official CAT communications, including the existing identity-verification requirements.

articles.title: IIT Kharagpur plans postgraduate medical education programmes
articles.summary: IIT Kharagpur is set to offer NMC-accredited postgraduate medical degrees, with 12 seats across six specialisations through NEET-PG counselling, according to the published report.
body: IIT Kharagpur is preparing to offer postgraduate medical education programmes, according to a report published on 13 November 2026. The development would add a medical-education pathway at an institution more widely known for its engineering and technology programmes.

The report says the proposed offering includes 12 seats across six specialisations and that admissions are to take place through NEET-PG counselling. It also describes the degrees as accredited by the National Medical Commission.

Prospective applicants should wait for the institute's official admission notice and the relevant counselling information to confirm the specialisations, eligibility conditions, seat matrix and admission schedule.

articles.title: Indian students win five medals at Junior Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad
articles.summary: India's five-member team won two gold, two silver and one bronze medal at the 2026 international junior Olympiad in Thailand. Students from Puducherry, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra were among the medal winners.
body: India's team secured five medals at the 2026 Junior Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad held in Thailand. The reported medal tally comprises two gold medals, two silver medals and one bronze medal.

The result highlights the performance of Indian school-level participants in an international academic competition focused on astronomy and astrophysics. The reported medal winners came from Puducherry, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra.

The achievement is a notable result for India's junior science-competition contingent. This report records the medal tally and locations reported by the cited news source; further participant details should be confirmed against the organisers' official results.

articles.title: IIT Roorkee opens registration for winter AI training programmes
articles.summary: IIT Roorkee's EICT Academy is offering six-week online winter programmes covering areas such as generative AI, machine learning, data science, full-stack development and edge AI. The reported application deadline is 30 November, with batches starting on 14 December and 4 January. Check programme details and fees directly with the academy before making a decision.
body: IIT Roorkee's EICT Academy has announced six-week online winter training programmes in technology-related subjects. The reported areas include generative artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, full-stack development and edge AI.

The published programme information gives 30 November 2026 as the application deadline and lists batches beginning on 14 December and 4 January. The available report describes the courses as online programmes with a six-week duration.

Prospective applicants should verify the exact course syllabus, eligibility, fees, certificate conditions and schedule with the academy before applying. These details can vary between individual programmes, and the news summary should not be treated as a substitute for the academy's current terms.

articles.title: WBCHSE publishes final HS Semester 3 answer keys
articles.summary: The West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education has released subject-wise final answer keys for the 2027 HS Semester 3 examination. The published keys reportedly identify three questions—one each in English, Chemistry and Biology—with no correct option. Students should check the council website for the official PDFs and the forthcoming result announcement.
body: The West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education has published final answer keys for the 2027 Higher Secondary Semester 3 examinations. The keys provide the council's final responses for the relevant objective questions.

Reporting on the release states that three questions—one each in English, Chemistry and Biology—were identified as having no correct option. Students should refer to the council's subject-wise final documents for the official treatment of those questions.
The answer-key publication is separate from the declaration of results. Students should rely on announcements from WBCHSE for the confirmed result date and any further examination-related notice.

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir sets 25% domicile reservation in private university admissions
articles.summary: The newly notified J&K Private Universities Rules 2026 require private universities to reserve at least 25% of student seats for Union Territory domiciles. The same minimum applies to teaching and non-teaching posts; the rules also establish an approval and regulatory framework for private institutions.
body: Jammu and Kashmir has notified the Private Universities Rules 2026, introducing a regulatory framework for private universities in the Union Territory. The rules include provisions concerning admissions and staffing.

According to the reported provisions, private universities must reserve at least 25 per cent of student seats for eligible Union Territory domiciles. A similar minimum reservation requirement is reported for teaching and non-teaching positions.

The rules also set out an approval and regulatory framework for private institutions. Universities and applicants should consult the notified rules for the precise scope, definitions, procedures and any conditions attached to these requirements.

articles.title: CBSE publishes Class 10 and Class 12 board exam date sheets for 2027
articles.summary: CBSE has published the 2027 main examination timetables for Classes 10 and 12. Students should consult the official PDF for their subject-wise dates, timings and examination instructions, and confirm any updates directly with the board.
body: The Central Board of Secondary Education has published the main examination date sheets for Class 10 and Class 12 for 2027. The schedules provide the subject-wise examination dates for the two board classes.

Students should use the official date-sheet document to confirm the date and timing for each of their subjects. They should also read the examination instructions included by the board rather than relying only on brief summaries.

Schools and students should continue to check official CBSE announcements for any later correction or update. The date sheet linked in the source record is the board-issued document for this examination session.

articles.title: CBSE releases subject-wise marks bifurcation for Classes 10 and 12
articles.summary: A new CBSE circular dated 6 November sets out subject-wise theory, practical, project and internal-assessment marks for the 2026–27 examination session. Students should check the entries for their own subjects in the official circular.
body: CBSE has issued a subject-wise marks-bifurcation circular for Classes 10 and 12 for the 2026–27 academic session. The document sets out how marks are allocated across the assessment components for the listed subjects.

The circular includes the distribution between theory examinations and applicable practical, project or internal-assessment components. The exact structure can differ by subject, so students should not assume that one subject follows the same pattern as another.

Students should consult the official circular and identify the entry for each subject they study. The board-issued document should be treated as the reference if a school handout or third-party summary appears different.

articles.title: NMMSS scholarship applications now close on 15 November
articles.summary: The Ministry of Education has extended the 2026–27 application deadline to 15 November. Key points: eligible students must complete One-Time Registration on the National Scholarship Portal; institute verification is due by 30 November and district verification by 15 December. The scheme offers ₹12,000 per year to selected eligible students.
body: The Ministry of Education has extended the application deadline for the 2026–27 National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) to 15 November 2026. The extension gives eligible applicants additional time to complete the required application process.

Applicants must complete One-Time Registration on the National Scholarship Portal. The published schedule also sets 30 November as the institute-verification deadline and 15 December as the district-verification deadline.

The scheme provides ₹12,000 per year to students selected under its eligibility and selection rules. Applicants should check the official scholarship portal and scheme instructions for the applicable conditions and required documents.
